about: How long one conversation turn may run, in seconds ([[BUG-168]]). The
project half of a setting the framework ships a default for: `promptStream`
takes `timeout` per call and falls back to 600 when none is passed. This
project passed none, so every turn ran at a number nobody here chose, just
as `backends.json` records the model and ceiling once did.
WHY 600 STOPPED BEING HARMLESS. It was sized for a turn where the caller does
its own reading and writing. Since delegation ([[REQ-295]]) a worker's whole
run happens inside ONE of the caller's tool calls, so the worker spends the
caller's clock. On 2026-09-29, three of five consultant turns died at 600 s,
and every one of those three had delegated. Observed worker runs take
minutes, and a turn may delegate more than once.
WHY 1800, AND WHY THE PLATFORM CAN HOLD IT. The turn is driven inside the
route's streaming response; the junction Durable Object only takes short
append calls. Workers put no wall-clock limit on an invocation while its
client stays connected, so the clock is not what binds. CPU time is. Waiting
on the provider costs none, but every write re-validates the definition
(~80 ms, measured in BUG-6612c4b7), so a write-heavy half hour can pass the
paid plan's 30 s default. `wrangler.toml` raises `cpu_ms` to the plan maximum
for that reason, and it is billed only when used. Two things still end a turn
early, and both are already accounted for: the client disconnecting aborts
the turn by design, and an eviction on deploy leaves an open ledger row
([[REQ-306]]) and a pending prompt ([[BUG-121]]).
A CEILING CAN STILL BE REACHED, so reaching it is narrated rather than
silent: see `turn-clock-core.ts`. Raising this number treats the symptom.
The structural fix is a delegation the caller does not wait inside, and
that change belongs upstream.
